reconstruction.scope: Cattle Car Memorial to the Deportees, Yad Vashem: independent red-brown two-axle wooden wagon on the mapped truncated railway, with shallow barrel roof, closed sliding doors, recessed upper side vents, metal ribs/chassis, buffers/coupler and the distinctive raised end brake cabin with three inset windows, side access steps and handrails. A tapered steel cantilever truss, cross bracing, ties and rails continue toward the higher land end. No copied lettering, car interior, visitors, forest, plaques or independent campus structures.

No raised terrain, invented pier or precinct flattening. Standard hill does not supply the exact excavated bank/cliff or track bed; inspect exposed truss, land attachment and approach before activation. Use the existing replaceRoads outline over the two authored disused rail ways, including their shared connected approach. After successful model loading only, suppress the covered bridge/rail visual; failed loading keeps it. Preserve original input data and every unrelated road/path. No terrain cutout or height modification. Corrected native whole/side/cabin/under-truss views inspected during this authoring pass. Approximate exterior fit accepted: the truncated western end stays elevated, open trusses enter the retained bank toward higher land, and the far rail end meets native grade at the working0.35m lift. Existing replaceRoads removes the duplicate procedural bridge/connected rail approach only after load. Original terrain, unrelated roads/paths and buildings remain intact. The coarse hill partly buries the deeper landward truss; exact historical cliff, bank excavation, pedestrian clearance and track-bed engineering are unverified.
